rv.q: Together, they’ve made a tight, sleek and personable evening.
This new show is a departure for Cohen, a ratcheting up of ambition for one of the most charismatic musical comedians of the past decade.

Broad Strokes often resembles a greatest-hits reel of Cohen's classic comedic interests, yet it's most engaging when Cat Cohen, author, is seriously pushing the persona of Cat Cohen against the sieve of being a serious adult.
It’s a hilarious Millennial saga and a great way to spend sixty-five minutes laughing your ass off.
Serving the raunch, Broad Strokes is a tour de force by a beloved diva high on confessional musical comedy and an intoxicating pop score.
That inspired conflict takes the audience through several stages of comic nirvana.
It’s safe to say that Broad Strokes is the funniest show you’ll ever see about a near-death experience.

So, in one of the seven original musical numbers in the show, Cohen sings: “Why not let Dr. Love fill the hole where my heart should beIt won’t be the worst thing a man has ever done to me.” And that’s not all: To avoid opening her chest for the operation, the surgeon accessed her heart through an artery in her groin.
But at 65 minutes, Broad Strokes feels a bit slight for a full off-Broadway production.
A curious visual decision, perhaps, but Cohen’s humorous matters of life or death certainly deserve some other-worldly grandeur.
In Broad Strokes, Cat Cohen turns her scariest year into the tightest set of her career—proof that the best material really is the stuff you didn't ask for.
Her tunes have a bouncy pleasantness to them, but also give the feeling of Kapwing- or Suno-generated tunes that set text messages to music.
Audience members experiencing a Cohen performance for the first time might find Broad Strokes somewhat superficial.

cn.t: Cohen transforms her stroke at 30 into a funny, chic cabaret that critics find entertaining if occasionally shallow. Praised for her wit and glamorous persona, though some note the show's brevity leaves the trauma feeling under-explored.
